messages:
nina_product: FYI — enterprise customer reported a bunch of 502/504s and huge latency spikes. They say requests should go to us-east-1 but traffic shows up in eu-1. Suspect client is sending conflicting region info.

alan_support: can you paste an example request (sanitized) + a request_id?

nina_product: request_id: req_01GZXK2J9QX0TQ0Y7A4H1Z2B
Here's the curl they used (tokens scrubbed):

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-east-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'
```

They claim our SDK used to only send the query param, but a newer client lib adds `X-Redwood-Region` header. Customer expects query param to take precedence.

kai_infra: digging into edge-router logs for that req_id now. quick note: our routing precedence config file is `router.priority = [header, query_param, account_default]` — header wins today.

lena_devex: oof. our SDK docs say "region param (query) overrides any header" — that mismatch would explain the surprise. Docs + runtime disagree.

sam_sre: can you paste a small excerpt from the edge decision log? even 3 lines around req_id will help.

nina_product: pasted below (redacted IPs):
```
2026-01-12T14:12:31Z req=req_01GZXK2J9QX0TQ0Y7A4H1Z2B src=1.2.3.4 header_region=eu-1 param_region=us-east-1 account=acme-prod route_selected=eu-1 latency_ms=2425
2026-01-12T14:12:31Z req=req_01GZXK2J9QX0TQ0Y7A4H1Z2B fallback_attempt=us-east-1 fallback_reason=capacity_unavailable
```

alan_support: so router honored header and then attempted fallback to param region when eu capacity hit, causing extra latency and errors. Also billing shows cross-region transfer cost for those tokens.

lena_devex: SDK shipped a change three weeks ago that starts injecting `X-Redwood-Region` for env compatibility with internal hosts. I can open a patch to stop sending header when `region` query param is set.

kai_infra: short-term mitigation: I can update edge to prefer `query_param` over `header` for 24h while we coordinate. Will push a rolling change but request a quick rollback plan.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: router-priority-override -> prefer-query-param (canary -> 3 regions). CHANGE_ID=deploy_7861

sam_sre: also enable decision-echo on the edge for that account so we can verify in real-time. I'll collect tcpdump if needed.

nina_product: I've told the customer we're patching the edge routing priority and that a SDK patch is coming. They want an ETA on billing credit for cross-region tokens.

alan_support: escalate billing to finance_team — include request_id and estimated token count (round up). I'll flag as P2 and ask for temporary credit while we remediate.

lena_devex: PR opened to SDK repo: stop-sending-region-header-if-param-present. Patch will go out to npm/pypi after tests. ETA ~ 4 hours.

kai_infra: canary is live in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 now. Monitoring :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary pass -> promotion started. CHANGE_ID=deploy_7861.rolled

sam_sre: observing no further reqs routed to eu-1 for this account when param=us-east-1. Latency back to normal for new requests. Will close once billing notified.

alan_support: billing contacted and notified. Finance acknowledged, asked for final token counts to finalize credit.

nina_product: customer confirmed new requests are hitting us-east-1 and latency is fixed. They're happy with temporary credit option.

lena_devex: SDK patch released to npm (v2.4.7) and PyPI (2.4.7). Docs updated to explicitly say "query param takes precedence".

kai_infra: follow-up action items: 1) reconcile router.default precedence in ops repo (now doc-aligned), 2) add unit test for header/param precedence, 3) add telemetry metric when both header+param present. I'll create tickets.

alan_support: thanks team. closing thread once finance confirms credit issued. :white_check_mark:
